laws.name: Lov om norsk statsborgerskap (statsborgerloven), LOV-2005-06-10-51
laws.articles: § 4 (acquisition at birth), § 22 a (re-acquisition by notification), § 24 (loss at 22 for absence), § 37 (transitional, children born before 1 Sept 2006); in force 1 Sept 2006; last amended by LOV-2024-12-20-81
laws.quote: § 4. Erverv ved fødsel Barn blir norsk statsborger ved fødselen dersom faren eller moren er norsk statsborger og foreldreskapet følger av barneloven. [EN gloss: A child becomes a Norwegian citizen at birth if the father or the mother is a Norwegian citizen and parentage follows from the Children Act.]

laws.name: Forskrift om erverv og tap av norsk statsborgerskap (statsborgerforskriften), FOR-2006-06-30-756
laws.articles: §§ 9-1 to 9-3 (residence and 'sufficient ties' for keeping citizenship after 22)
laws.quote: Søkere som før fylte 22 år har opphold i Norge på til sammen 6 måneder, skal anses for å ha tilstrekkelig tilknytning. [EN: Applicants who before turning 22 have stayed in Norway for a total of 6 months shall be considered to have sufficient ties.]

rules.rule: Born on or after 1 September 2006 anywhere in the world to a Norwegian mother or father (married or not): Norwegian at birth, automatically. Only the parent's citizenship AT THE CHILD'S BIRTH counts; there is no ancestry claim through grandparents unless the parent was still Norwegian when the child was born.
rules.quote: If you were born on 1 September 2006 or later and you have a Norwegian mother or father , you automatically became a Norwegian citizen at birth. This applies regardless of whether you were born in Norway or abroad, and regardless of whether or not your parents were married.

rules.rule: Born before 1 September 2006: Norwegian at birth if the mother was Norwegian, or the father was Norwegian AND married to the mother at the birth (or died before the birth while Norwegian and married). Child of an unmarried Norwegian father and foreign mother: not automatic; could only become Norwegian by notification before age 18 (§ 37).
rules.quote: If you were born before 1 September 2006, you became a Norwegian citizen at birth if your mother was Norwegian, or your father was Norwegian and was married to your mother when you were born, or your father died before you were born, but was a Norwegian citizen and married to your mother at the time of his death. If your father was Norwegian, but he was not married to your mother, you did not automatically become a Norwegian citizen. However, until you turned 18, you could easily become a Norwegian citizen by handing in a notification of Norwegian citizenship.

rules.rule: Norwegian mother married to a foreign father, child born before 1 July 1979: per UDI's official self-check, a child born 1 Jan 1951 - 30 June 1961 in that situation is NOT Norwegian; a child born 1 July 1961 - 30 June 1979 only became Norwegian if the mother filed a notification after 1 July 1979 and before the child turned 18. Checker: route these users to 'contact UDI', not to a yes.
rules.quote: Has your mother submitted a notification and received a certificate of citizenship for children with a Norwegian mother after 1 July 1979 and before you turned 18? [...] If you were born before 1979 and you are uncertain about whether you became a Norwegian citizen at birth, you can contact UDI for more information.

rules.rule: Norwegian at birth but never resided in Norway for 2 years in total (or 7 years in total in Norway + other Nordic countries): citizenship is lost automatically on the 22nd birthday, unless an application to keep it is filed BEFORE turning 22 (late filing accepted only if not seriously at fault). Six months' total stay in Norway before 22 counts as sufficient ties (stays of at least 6 continuous months count as residence). When a parent loses citizenship this way, the children lose it too unless the other parent is still Norwegian. Never applies if it would make the person stateless.
rules.quote: § 24. Tap ved fravær fra riket Den som ervervet norsk statsborgerskap ved fødselen, men som ikke har vært bosatt i til sammen to år i Norge eller til sammen syv år i Norge og andre nordiske land, taper sitt norske statsborgerskap når vedkommende fyller 22 år. Den som ellers ville tape sitt norske statsborgerskap etter første ledd, kan etter søknad få rett til å beholde det såfremt søkeren har tilstrekkelig tilknytning til Norge. Søknad om det må fremmes innen vedkommende fyller 22 år. [EN: Whoever acquired Norwegian citizenship at birth but has not resided for a total of two years in Norway, or a total of seven years in Norway and other Nordic countries, loses Norwegian citizenship on turning 22. A person who would otherwise lose it may on application keep it if they have sufficient ties to Norway. The application must be made before turning 22.]

rules.rule: Former Norwegian citizens who lost citizenship by acquiring another citizenship (e.g. US naturalization) before 1 January 2020, or by failing to renounce a previous citizenship, have a right to re-acquire it by simple notification (no residence in Norway needed). Conditions: identity verified (normally passport); if Norwegian by birth, at least 6 months in total in Norway before age 22 (several short stays/holidays may be added up); no disqualifying criminal record (police certificate if over 15); the loss must first be registered in the National Population Register. Not available to people who lost citizenship at 22 for lack of residence. No deadline appears in § 22 a.
rules.quote: You must have lost your Norwegian citizenship for one of these reasons you became a citizen of another country before 1 January 2020, or you became a Norwegian citizen after applying for it, but you did not renounce your previous citizenship by the deadline you received from UDI. [...] You cannot have lost Norwegian citizenship because you did not live long enough in Norway before you turned 22. [...] If you became a Norwegian citizen when you were born, you must have stayed in Norway for a total of six months before you turned 22. These six months can consist of several short stays/holidays.

rules.rule: Statutory basis of the notification route (chapter 4 A, in force 1 January 2020).
rules.quote: § 22 a. Gjenerverv av norsk statsborgerskap ved melding Den som har tapt norsk statsborgerskap ved erverv av et annet statsborgerskap, eller ved manglende løsning fra et annet statsborgerskap, har ved melding rett til å bli norsk statsborger. [...] Melderen må sannsynliggjøre å ha hatt opphold i Norge på til sammen seks måneder før fylte 22 år. Dette kravet gjelder ikke meldere som tidligere har ervervet norsk statsborgerskap ved søknad. [EN: A person who lost Norwegian citizenship by acquiring another citizenship, or by not being released from another citizenship, has by notification the right to become a Norwegian citizen. [...] The person must show it is likely they stayed in Norway for a total of six months before turning 22. This does not apply to those who earlier acquired Norwegian citizenship by application.]

rules.rule: Norway has no citizenship-by-ancestry route for grandchildren or later generations living abroad: transmission is only from a parent who is Norwegian at the child's birth (§ 4). Descendants who do not qualify are directed to apply for citizenship (residence-based) or a residence permit for those who had a Norwegian parent.
rules.quote: If you do not meet the requirements for becoming a Norwegian citizen, you may apply for a residence permit for those who had a Norwegian parent when they were born .

procedure.authority: UDI (Utlendingsdirektoratet, Norwegian Directorate of Immigration); documents handed in at a Norwegian foreign service mission (in the US: Consulate General New York, San Francisco, or the Embassy in Washington) or the police in Norway
procedure.how: Former citizen in the US: (1) have the US citizenship registered in the Norwegian National Population Register (Skatteetaten); (2) fill in the UDI online notification and pay the fee; (3) obtain a Norwegian police certificate (politiattest) with purpose 'Notification of re-acquisition of Norwegian citizenship'; (4) book an appointment at the consulate/embassy and bring originals + copies of all checklist documents. Person born abroad to a Norwegian parent: apply for a Norwegian passport at a mission; before age 22 file an application to keep citizenship if § 24 residence is not met.

documents.note: As a rule a passport is required

documents.item: Certificate of Naturalization + US passport copy (to register the US citizenship in Folkeregisteret)
documents.note: Sent to Skatteetaten by mail or online before the police certificate is ordered

documents.item: Norwegian police certificate (politiattest), for applicants over 15
documents.note: If not in the population register: proof of former citizenship (expired Norwegian passport, birth/baptismal certificate) is needed to order it

documents.item: Originals and same-size copies of all checklist documents (some checklists ask for passports from the last 10 years with all stamped pages)
documents.note: The consulate cannot make copies; do not staple. UDI checklist sets apostille/translation requirements per document (not captured here)

processing_time.label: Notification of citizenship for former Norwegian citizens
processing_time.quote: It normally takes 3 months from the time you deliver the documents to the police or the Norwegian foreign service mission until you receive a reply.
processing_time.published_or_updated: last updated 24 September 2026, next update 29 October 2026

processing_time.label: Application to keep Norwegian citizenship
processing_time.quote: It normally takes 3 months from the time you deliver the documents to the police or the Norwegian foreign service mission until you receive a reply.

dual_citizenship.note: Allowed since 1 January 2020; no need to tell Norwegian authorities you keep your other citizenship.
dual_citizenship.quote: From 1 January 2020, it is allowed to have one or more citizenships in addition to a Norwegian citizenship. [...] You do not have to inform Norwegian authorities that you wish to keep your previous citizenship.

other_requirements.item: Loss of citizenship (if acquired a foreign citizenship before 2020) must be registered in the National Population Register before filing
other_requirements.quote: This must be properly registered before delivering the notification of citizenship.

other_requirements.item: Military service obligation in principle applies to Norwegian citizens
other_requirements.quote: In principle, as a Norwegian citizen, you are obliged to serve your military service in Norway, but the rules vary depending on which other country you are a citizen of.

recent_changes.what: Dual citizenship allowed; former § 23 (loss on voluntary acquisition of foreign citizenship) repealed; chapter 4 A (§ 22 a re-acquisition by notification) added (LOV-2018-12-20-121).
Latest amendment to the Act recorded on Lovdata (LOV-2024-12-20-81); no change found to §§ 4, 22 a or 24 affecting descent claims.
Nothing found that moved in 2026 for descent/re-acquisition rules. Waiting time for former-citizen notifications: 3 months (24 Sept 2026).

open_questions: Brief mentions a declaration route with a 31 Dec 2022 deadline: current § 22 a contains no deadline and UDI's page states none. A temporary transitional rule for children of re-acquirers (2020-2022, reported by secondary sources) was not found in the current consolidated Act; not confirmed on an official page.

Full pre-1979 historical matrix (births before 1951, born to unmarried Norwegian mother, effect of parent's pre-2020 naturalization on minor children) is only partly verified via UDI's interactive guide; route these cases to 'contact UDI'.
Apostille/translation requirements per document are in the UDI checklist generated per case; not captured.
